title: Penchick and Chloe's Trees
statementMd:
With just a few hours left until Penchick and Chloe leave for Singapore, they could hardly wait to see the towering trees at the Singapore Botanic Gardens! Attempting to contain their excitement, Penchick crafted a rooted tree to keep Chloe and himself busy.

Penchick has a rooted tree$^{\text{∗}}$ consisting of $n$ vertices, numbered from $1$ to $n$, with vertex $1$ as the root, and Chloe can select a non-negative integer $d$ to create a perfect binary tree$^{\text{†}}$ of depth $d$.

Since Penchick and Chloe are good friends, Chloe wants her tree to be isomorphic$^{\text{‡}}$ to Penchick's tree. To meet this condition, Chloe can perform the following operation on her own tree any number of times:

- Select an edge $(u,v)$, where $u$ is the parent of $v$.
- Remove vertex $v$ and all the edges connected to $v$, then connect all of $v$'s previous children directly to $u$.

In particular, doing an operation on an edge $(u, v)$ where $v$ is a leaf will delete vertex $v$ without adding any new edges.

Since constructing a perfect binary tree can be time-consuming, Chloe wants to choose the minimum $d$ such that a perfect binary tree of depth $d$ can be made isomorphic to Penchick's tree using the above operation. Note that she can't change the roots of the trees.

$^{\text{∗}}$A tree is a connected graph without cycles. A rooted tree is a tree where one vertex is special and called the root. The parent of vertex $v$ is the first vertex on the simple path from $v$ to the root. The root has no parent. A child of vertex $v$ is any vertex $u$ for which $v$ is the parent. A leaf is any vertex without children. $^{\text{†}}$A full binary tree is rooted tree, in which each node has $0$ or $2$ children. A perfect binary tree is a full binary tree in which every leaf is at the same distance from the root. The depth of such a tree is the distance from the root to a leaf.$^{\text{‡}}$Two rooted trees, rooted at $r_1$ and $r_2$ respectively, are considered isomorphic if there exists a permutation $p$ of the vertices such that an edge $(u, v)$ exists in the first tree if and only if the edge $(p_u, p_v)$ exists in the second tree, and $p_{r_1} = r_2$.

## Input

Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $t$ ($1 \le t \le 10^5$). The description of the test cases follows.

The first line of each test case contains a single integer $n$ ($2 \le n \le 10^6$) — the number of vertices in Penchick's tree.

The second line of each test case contains $n-1$ integers $p_2, p_3, \ldots, p_n$ ($1 \leq p_i \leq i-1$) — the parent of vertex $i$.

It is guaranteed that the sum of $n$ over all test cases does not exceed $10^6$.

## Output

For each test case, output a single integer on each line: the minimum depth of Chloe's perfect binary tree.

## Note

For the first test case, create a perfect binary tree with depth $2$.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/8d42bd7999c3041650dc035cbfa71627f0c6983a.png)

Consider carrying out the operation on edge $AC$. Then the edges $AC$, $CF$, and $CG$ are removed, and edges $AF$ and $AG$ are added.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/4c459430fe1a6b01a84920a49fdb9eb61a3d3261.png)

The resulting tree is isomorphic to the tree given in the input. It can be proven that no sequence of operations carried out on a binary tree of depth less than $2$ can lead to a tree isomorphic to the tree given in the input.

In the second test case, the tree is already isomorphic to a perfect binary tree of depth $3$.
statementZhMd:
距离 Penchick 和 Chloe 动身前往新加坡只剩几个小时了，他们已经迫不及待想去新加坡植物园看看高耸的树木！为了平复激动的心情，Penchick 构造了一棵有根树，让 Chloe 和自己有事可做。

Penchick 有一棵包含 $n$ 个顶点的有根树$^{\text{∗}}$，顶点编号为 $1$ 到 $n$，其中顶点 $1$ 是根。Chloe 可以选择一个非负整数 $d$，构造一棵深度为 $d$ 的完美二叉树$^{\text{†}}$。

Penchick 和 Chloe 是好朋友，因此 Chloe 希望自己的树与 Penchick 的树同构$^{\text{‡}}$。为满足这一条件，Chloe 可以在自己的树上进行任意次数的以下操作：

- 选择一条边 $(u,v)$，其中 $u$ 是 $v$ 的父亲。
- 删除顶点 $v$ 以及与 $v$ 相连的所有边，然后将 $v$ 原来的所有子节点直接连接到 $u$。

特别地，如果对一条边 $(u, v)$ 执行操作，且 $v$ 是叶子，那么会删除顶点 $v$，而不会添加任何新边。

由于构造完美二叉树可能很耗时，Chloe 想选择最小的 $d$，使得可以通过上述操作将一棵深度为 $d$ 的完美二叉树变成与 Penchick 的树同构的树。注意，她不能改变树的根。

$^{\text{∗}}$树是一个连通且无环的图。有根树是指定一个顶点为根的树。顶点 $v$ 的父亲是从 $v$ 到根的简单路径上的第一个顶点。根没有父亲。顶点 $v$ 的子节点是所有以 $v$ 为父亲的顶点。没有子节点的顶点称为叶子。$^{\text{†}}$满二叉树是一棵有根树，其中每个节点有 $0$ 个或 $2$ 个子节点。完美二叉树是一棵满二叉树，其中所有叶子到根的距离都相同。这种树的深度是根到叶子的距离。$^{\text{‡}}$若存在一个从顶点到顶点的置换 $p$，使得第一棵树中存在边 $(u, v)$ 当且仅当第二棵树中存在边 $(p_u, p_v)$，且 $p_{r_1} = r_2$，则称两棵分别以 $r_1$ 和 $r_2$ 为根的有根树同构。

## 输入格式

每个输入包含多组测试用例。第一行包含测试用例数量 $t$（$1 \le t \le 10^5$）。接下来是各测试用例的描述。

每个测试用例的第一行包含一个整数 $n$（$2 \le n \le 10^6$）——Penchick 的树中的顶点数。

每个测试用例的第二行包含 $n-1$ 个整数 $p_2, p_3, \ldots, p_n$（$1 \leq p_i \leq i-1$）——顶点 $i$ 的父亲。

保证所有测试用例的 $n$ 之和不超过 $10^6$。

## 输出格式

对于每个测试用例，在单独一行输出一个整数：Chloe 的完美二叉树的最小深度。

## 说明

对于第一个测试用例，构造一棵深度为 $2$ 的完美二叉树。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/8d42bd7999c3041650dc035cbfa71627f0c6983a.png)

考虑对边 $AC$ 执行操作。此时边 $AC$、$CF$ 和 $CG$ 会被删除，并添加边 $AF$ 和 $AG$。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/4c459430fe1a6b01a84920a49fdb9eb61a3d3261.png)

得到的树与输入中的树同构。可以证明，对深度小于 $2$ 的二叉树进行任何操作，都无法得到与输入中的树同构的树。

在第二个测试用例中，这棵树已经与一棵深度为 $3$ 的完美二叉树同构。
